page: Microsoft Azure E4s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores via hyperthreading at a clock rate of 4.2 GHz. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation that fits standard memory-intensive profiles. The processor integrates advanced feature sets including AVX-512, Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for tile and INT8 math, and cryptographic acceleration extensions. The instance carries no local storage and does not include hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Benchmark outcomes show varied performance characteristics across workloads. Single-threaded gzip compression achieves strong performance in the top 25% at 32.55 GB/sec, while single-core stress-ng registers average throughput of 2034.29. Multi-core performance is limited by the 2 physical core count, posting a weak score of 4104.86 in stress-ng and 26.16 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. PassMark CPU and memory metrics land in the middle tier, with a PassMark CPU score of 8645.74 and memory score of 2294.39. Redis performance achieves an average rate of 8.21 million SET operations per second, whereas PassMark database operations and multi-threaded decompression fall into lower percentiles.

Because the E4s_v7 offers 32 GB of RAM on a 4-vCPU footprint, it functions efficiently for memory-resident tasks without requiring high vCPU licensing overhead. The primary tradeoff lies in raw multi-core throughput and storage configuration, as the instance lacks integrated local disks and relies on network-attached storage. The hardware architecture best fits medium-scale in-memory caches, enterprise applications requiring a 1:8 core-to-memory ratio, lightweight data transformations, and moderate web services.
description: Microsoft Azure E4s_v7 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, driven by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, it incorporates AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions while omitting local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place single-threaded compression in the upper tier at 32.55 GB/sec, alongside middle-tier PassMark CPU and memory scores. Multi-core compute performance reflects the 2-core physical limit, yielding lower relative throughput in multi-threaded stress-ng and compression tests. Its 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation offers cost efficiency for memory-heavy operations, suiting Redis caching, in-memory processing, and general enterprise memory-bound workloads.
